notes.b: Resource management is the planned use of the resources a family has available to reach its goals.
points: Resources are anything a family can draw on to meet its needs and wants.
Human resources: the time, energy, skills and knowledge of family members.
Material resources: equipment, food, ingredients, clothing, furniture and other household goods.
Economic resources: income, savings and credit available to the family.
Environmental resources: the physical surroundings and community facilities that support family life, such as space, daylight and local services.
The core purpose is to use available resources efficiently in order to achieve goals.
A second purpose is to improve the quality of family life, and to enable each family member to reach their full potential.
Good management reduces waste of time, money, food and energy.

notes.b: A management system is a planned, step-by-step way of turning a need or goal into a result using the resources available.
points: A management system lets a family decide what needs doing, who does it, when it is done and which resources it needs.
Everyday tasks that use a management system include meal planning, budgeting, housework, childcare and shopping.
One-off events such as a birthday party, a holiday or a house move also use a management system.
Systems work best when the goals, standards and responsibilities are agreed in advance, so that members know what is expected of them.
Systems are not fixed: they are adjusted when circumstances change, such as a new job or the arrival of a baby.

notes.h: How good management contributes to a well-run home
points: Planned routines make sure meals, laundry and school preparation are done on time, with less last-minute stress.
Meal plans and shopping lists reduce impulse buying and the amount of food that is wasted.
Shared tasks spread the workload fairly, so no single member carries the whole household.
Goals and standards agreed by all members give the family a shared direction and reduce conflict.
Efficient use of time and equipment frees time for leisure, rest and relationships.
Careful use of energy and water lowers the cost of running the home.

notes.h: The family as a managerial unit
notes.b: The family is a small group that pools, allocates and controls its own resources.
points: Article 41 of the Irish Constitution recognises the family as the natural, primary and fundamental unit group of society.
Each member contributes resources such as earnings, time or skills, and each member benefits from the shared pool.
Adults usually plan and coordinate; children and teenagers take on tasks and share in decisions as they grow older.
Family goals may be short term, such as a weekly shop or a family outing, or long term, such as buying a home or saving for education.
Management requires balancing individual wants against the needs and goals of the household as a whole.

keyTerms.definition: Anything a family can draw on to meet its needs and wants.
The efficient use of available resources to achieve the goals of the family.
The time, energy, skills and knowledge of the people in a family.
The equipment, food, goods and other physical items a family uses in the home.
The income, savings and credit available to a family to pay for what it needs.
The physical surroundings and community facilities that support family life.
A planned, step-by-step way of turning a need or goal into a result using available resources.
A group, such as the family, that plans and controls its own resources.

factCards.definition: Human (time, energy, skills, knowledge), material (equipment, food, goods), economic (income, savings, credit) and environmental (space, facilities, surroundings).

factCards.term: Two aims of family resource management
factCards.definition: To use available resources efficiently to achieve goals; to improve the quality of family life.

factCards.term: Three benefits of a planned household routine
factCards.definition: Tasks are completed on time with less stress; time and money are not wasted on last-minute decisions; the workload is shared fairly.

factCards.definition: Meal planning, budgeting, housework and childcare.

questions.prompt: Outline the purpose of family resource management and give one example of how a family can use its resources efficiently.
questions.model: Purpose, any two points at 2 marks each (4 marks): to use available resources efficiently in order to achieve goals; to improve the quality of family life; to enable each family member to reach their full potential. Example (2 marks): a weekly meal plan with a shopping list uses money and time efficiently and reduces food waste.

questions.prompt: Discuss how a family, acting as a managerial unit, uses its resources to achieve its goals. Refer to the types of resource and to the goals a family may set in your answer.
questions.model: Family as a managerial unit: the family pools its income, time, skills and goods and decides how they are allocated. Types of resource: human (time, energy, skills, knowledge), material (equipment, food, goods), economic (income, savings, credit) and environmental (space, facilities, surroundings). Goals: short term, such as a weekly shop or an outing, and long term, such as buying a home or saving for education. Process: adults plan and coordinate; children and teenagers take on tasks and share in decisions as they grow older. Management system: tasks, responsibilities and standards are agreed in advance and the plan is adjusted when circumstances change. Balance: individual wants must be weighed against the needs and goals of the household as a whole. Outcome: resources are used efficiently, waste is reduced and the quality of family life improves.
